close_reason: Fixed in de2b2df. Added #[non_exhaustive] to OpResult plus typed constructors OpResult::ok(op_index, id: Option<Id>) and OpResult::err(op_index, error: SetError). External consumers MUST use the constructors; field-init is forbidden outside the defining crate. Within crate-jmap-chat-server the existing field-init in memory.rs:1205 is kept (still valid within the defining crate; migrating would require destructuring the Result outcome with no benefit). Pre-1.0 / pre-publish; additive #[non_exhaustive] is free.
description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:53-59

  #[derive(Debug)]
  pub struct OpResult {
      pub op_index: usize,
      pub outcome: Result<Option<jmap_types::Id>, SetError>,
  }

OpResult is constructed BY consumer backends inside their
ChatBackend::apply_space_patch implementation, then returned to the
kit's handle_space_set handler for mapping into the /set response.
This is a true two-way contract: consumers both construct and the
kit consumes.

The struct has two pub fields and is NOT #[non_exhaustive]. Future
non-breaking additions are impossible without a major bump:

- An audit-log handle to thread through to the consumer's transport
  for push events.
- A timestamp/lease-token field for transactional backends that
  want to expose commit ordering.
- A diagnostic-only "would this op have succeeded under different
  permission set?" annotation for permission-tool consumers.

Compare with ChatLimits, EmojiSetOp — both #[non_exhaustive].

Fix:
  #[non_exhaustive]
  #[derive(Debug)]
  pub struct OpResult { ... }

  impl OpResult {
      pub fn ok(op_index: usize, id: Option<Id>) -> Self { ... }
      pub fn err(op_index: usize, e: SetError) -> Self { ... }
  }

The constructor pair replaces the field-init shape so consumers do
not depend on positional field order. Per workspace AGENTS.md the
canonical-template sweep also lands the same pattern in
jmap-mail-server's equivalent type (none exists yet — first
strike).
